channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula faz giro pela Europa; viagem começa pela Espanha
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva begins his European tour this Friday (17) in Spain, attending the 1st Brazil–Spain Summit and meetings with business leaders, followed by a visit to Germany on April 19–20, where he will meet Chancellor Friedrich Merz and sign agreements on defense, AI, and infrastructure. The trip also includes participation in the Democracy Always Forum in Barcelona, aiming to strengthen democratic and commercial ties, with Spain being Brazil’s eighth-largest trading partner in 2024. Lula is expected to return to Brazil on Wednesday (22).

item.title: Ustra, cusparada, gângster e Tiririca: relembre 10 marcos da sessão do impeachment de Dilma
item.description: On April 17, 2016, the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies held the vote that opened the impeachment process against President Dilma Rousseff, with House President Eduardo Cunha repeatedly asking "How do you vote, deputy?" hundreds of times. The plenary was packed, and the session became infamous for moments such as Jair Bolsonaro’s "cusp" in tribute to Colonel Ustra, along with other incidents involving figures like Tiririca. The event was a symbolic and political milestone in the institutional crisis that led to Rousseff’s removal.

item.title: Tarcísio explica foto com funkeiro preso em operação da PF
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas responded to controversy over a photo with a funk singer arrested in a PF operation, stating he does not check criminal records before taking photos or attending events. He defended the approach as part of his routine of engaging with society without prior judgments.

item.title: ICE diz à PF que Ramagem pode aguardar conclusão do processo de asilo nos EUA em liberdade
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem was released from U.S. custody after applying for political asylum, according to ICE’s communication to the PF. His release occurred prior to a previously scheduled meeting between Brazilian and U.S. authorities aimed at discussing his case and preventing his release. The Brazilian government had hoped to keep him detained during deportation negotiations but now awaits updates on his immigration status.

item.title: Com saída de Odair ao TCU, PT irá à Justiça para manter vaga na Câmara
item.description: The PT is seeking judicial intervention to ensure that Gilmar Machado (PT), the second substitute of the Brazil of Hope federation, assumes the seat vacated by Odair Cunha in the Chamber of Deputies following his appointment to the TCU. The first substitute, Glaycon Franco, left the PV for the PSDB during the party window, which the PT argues disqualifies him from inheriting the mandate, maintaining that the seat belongs to the party, not the individual. The TSE and electoral precedents support this position, as the federation remained intact and the second substitute remained affiliated with the PT.

item.title: Representantes de Lula e Trump discutem investigação comercial dos EUA que inclui o Pix
item.description: Representatives from the Lula administration and the Trump government met in Washington to discuss the U.S. Section 301 trade investigation targeting Brazilian policies such as Pix and ethanol. Brazil provided technical clarifications without expecting immediate decisions and reiterated it will not alter Pix under external pressure. The government emphasized consensus-building, despite the recent passage of the Economic Reciprocity Law by Congress.

item.title: Tarcísio se manifesta sobre foto com funkeiro preso em operação da PF
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas commented on a photo showing him alongside Rodrigo Inácio de Lima Oliveira, founder of GR6 Explode, who was arrested in Operation Narco Fluxo on suspicion of money laundering linked to drug trafficking. Tarcísio stated he does not check criminal records when taking photos at events and emphasized the meeting was personal, not official, held in August 2024 at singer Latino’s residence, not on his official schedule.

item.title: Haddad estreia apelido para Flávio: 'o bolsonarinho'
item.description: Fernando Haddad responded to a post by Flávio Bolsonaro, who used images of people in vulnerable conditions — including children — from 2021, during the Bolsonaro government, falsely attributing them to Lula’s administration. Haddad posted a video on social media rebutting the misinformation and nicknamed Flávio 'the little Bolsonaro'.

item.title: Lula diz que Trump "não pode ficar ameaçando outros países com guerra o tempo todo"
item.description: President Lula criticized Donald Trump for constantly threatening other countries with war, stating he was not elected 'emperor of the world'. Lula said he had appealed to leaders like Xi Jinping, Putin, and Macron to convene a UN Security Council meeting on the Iran conflict, but received no response. He urged immediate reform of the UN Security Council to include permanent members from Africa, the Middle East, Brazil, and Germany, arguing that the current permanent members — the world’s largest arms producers and nuclear powers — undermine global peace.

item.title: Moçambicanos se inspiram no sistema de votação brasileiro e elogiam urna eletrônica
item.description: A delegation of five technicians from Mozambique's Constitutional Council visited Brazil's TSE to study the electronic voting system, praising its security, reliability and efficiency. They expressed interest in adopting the model in their country, emphasizing the need to strengthen democracy through advanced electoral technology. The visit was part of the Tobias Barreto exchange program, focused on digitalization and institutional strengthening between the two nations.

item.title: Em carta, Edegar Pretto diz que será vice de Juliana Brizola no RS
item.description: Edegar Pretto (PT) announced he will be the vice-gubernatorial candidate on Juliana Brizola's (PDT) ticket for the Rio Grande do Sul state government in 2026, following guidance from the state PT leadership, discussions with local figures, and a request from President Lula. He affirmed his commitment to progressive values and aims to strengthen Lula's political base in the state, marking the first time the PT will not field its own candidate for the Piratini Palace.

item.title: Por mais tempo para articular, governo avalia adiar sabatina de Messias
item.description: The Lula government is considering postponing Jorge Messias' STF confirmation hearing from Tuesday (April 28) to Wednesday (April 29) to gain more time for political negotiations with senators, aiming to avoid senator fatigue and potential lack of quorum in a same-day CCJ and plenary vote. The decision hinges on balancing attendance assurance with extended negotiation time, as approval remains uncertain with an expected tight vote.

item.title: Após ser solto, Ramagem diz que PF de Andrei Rodrigues é de “jagunços”
item.description: Former federal deputy Alexandre Ramagem (PL-RJ) was released after 48 hours in ICE custody in the U.S., following detention during a routine traffic stop. He accused the Brazilian Federal Police and its director-general, Andrei Rodrigues, of becoming a 'police of gunmen,' claiming his detention was unjust and that his U.S. status is fully regular. Ramagem thanked allies including Allan dos Santos, Eduardo Bolsonaro, Paulo Figueiredo, and Senator Hiran Gonçalves, and claimed that Trump administration officials intervened to secure his administrative release without bond or judicial proceedings.

item.title: Dallagnol ocupa 2º lugar nas pesquisas, mas está inelegível
item.description: Former federal deputy Deltan Dallagnol ranks second in Paraná Senate race polls with 28.2% voting intention, but remains ineligible until 2030 due to a TSE decision that annulled his candidacy in 2023. The Paraná Pesquisas survey, conducted April 10-12, 2026 with 1,500 respondents, shows ex-senator Alvaro Dias (MDB) leading with 44.5%. Dallagnol's ineligibility stems from the TSE's finding that his resignation as prosecutor was timed to avoid Ficha Clean Law sanctions.

item.title: SP deposita R$ 561 milhões para desapropriações do túnel Santos-Guarujá e cobra governo federal
item.description: The São Paulo government deposited R$ 561.89 million with Mota-Engil to fund expropriations and resettlements for the Santos-Guarujá tunnel project, as announced by the Tarcísio administration. The state also demanded the federal government fulfill its promised financial contributions to the infrastructure project linking the ports of Santos and Guarujá.

item.title: “Não pode ficar ameaçando outros países o tempo todo”, diz Lula sobre Trump
item.description: President Lula criticized Donald Trump for constantly threatening other countries with war, stating that Trump was not elected 'emperor of the world' and that such threats are unacceptable. He stressed the need for a world grounded in dialogue and mutual respect between nations.

item.title: Oposição perde ‘bala de prata’ e candidato do PL corre sozinho na eleição da Alerj
item.description: Judge Suely Lopes Magalhães denied the opposition's request for a secret ballot in the Alerj presidential election, preserving an open vote that favors Douglas Ruas (PL). The ruling shattered the opposition's last hope to block Ruas's ascent, as secret voting was seen as key to building an alternative candidacy free from party pressure. The court ruled that voting procedure is an internal legislative matter, not subject to judicial intervention, particularly after the STF clarified that the Alerj president does not automatically succeed the governor in case of vacancy.

item.title: USP teve ao menos 680 dias de paralisações em 3 décadas
item.description: Since 1995, the University of São Paulo (USP) has experienced at least 680 days of strikes, primarily over salaries, hiring, and working conditions. The latest strike began on April 14, 2026, by technical and administrative staff, later joined by students who added demands regarding student housing, university restaurants, and space management. The approval of GACE, a bonus for professors in March, has divided faculty and been criticized by unions for threatening salary equity.

item.title: Kalil eleito para a Academia Nacional de Medicina
item.description: Roberto Kalil, physician to Lula, president of the InCor Board at Hospital das Clínicas and general director of the Cardiology Center at Hospital Sírio-Libanês, has been elected to the National Academy of Medicine with 72 out of 96 possible votes. The achievement reflects his recognized expertise in cardiology and hospital management in Brazil.

item.title: O alerta dado pelo líder do PL no Senado a Jorge Messias, indicado por Lula ao STF
item.description: PL Senate leader Carlos Portinho met with Jorge Messias, Lula’s nominee to the STF, and reaffirmed his opposition to the appointment, stating he will not vote in favor. Portinho warned Messias about the unfavorable political climate, citing tensions between Congress and the STF due to the Organized Crime CPI, which voted to indict ministers of the Court, triggering defensiveness and corporatism among senators. The PL, with 32 senators, has closed ranks against the nomination, leaving Messias to seek the required votes solely from the government base.

item.title: Líder do PL diz que soltura de Ramagem nos EUA, detido com visto vencido, teve ajuda da Casa Branca
item.description: PL leader Sóstenes Cavalcante claimed that former deputy Alexandre Ramagem was released in the U.S. after two days of detention for an expired visa, thanks to White House assistance, citing Marco Rubio and Darren Beattie. Ramagem had been arrested by ICE following a traffic violation, with Brazilian authorities expecting his deportation to serve a sentence for his role in the coup plot. The PL is seeking political asylum for Ramagem in the U.S., arguing he faces judicial persecution in Brazil.

item.title: Flávio formaliza defesa no STF em inquérito por suposta calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro formally submitted his defense before the STF in an inquiry over alleged slander against President Lula, as ordered by Justice Alexandre de Moraes. His legal team will be led by the law firm Tracy Reinaldet Advogados Associados. The case unfolds amid heightened political tensions between the government and opposition.

item.title: Lula diz que Trump 'não pode ficar ameaçando outros países com guerra o tempo todo'
item.description: Lula criticized Donald Trump for constantly threatening other countries with war, stating Trump was not elected 'emperor of the world'. He advocated for UN Security Council reform to include more representatives from Africa, the Middle East, Brazil, and Germany, arguing that current permanent members are the world's top arms producers and drivers of global conflicts. Lula also said he had requested an emergency UN Security Council meeting on Iran with China, Russia, and France, but received no support.

item.title: Alckmin defende taxa das blusinhas e diz que não há decisão do governo sobre fim da medida
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin defended the 'blusinhas tax', arguing it protects national jobs by making Chinese imports less competitive than domestic production, despite criticism from President Lula and ministers like José Guimarães. He stated there is no current government decision to repeal the tax, which raised R$425 million in January 2026 — a 25% increase from January 2025 — and R$5 billion in 2025, supporting fiscal targets. Business groups and workers from 67 associations protested the potential repeal, calling it 'electoral'.

item.title: Lula critica Trump e diz que ex-presidente não é ‘imperador do mundo’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized Donald Trump for threatening other countries with war and stated that he 'was not elected emperor of the world'. Lula advocated for reforming the UN Security Council, urging meetings with leaders from China, Russia, and France to prevent conflict escalation, and warned that the poor in Africa and Latin America would bear the cost of wars initiated by powerful nations.

item.title: Articulação política de Lula assume foco no Senado e em Alcolumbre
item.description: Minister José Guimarães (PT) stated that the priority of the Secretariat of Institutional Relations is to recompose the government’s relationship with the Senate, focusing on dialogue with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to advance key agendas such as the Public Security PEC by July and the end of the 6X1 work schedule, following a period of strain that stalled relevant legislation.

item.title: Delegados da PF alertam Lula sobre 'extrema frustração' com compromisso descumprido
item.description: The National Association of Federal Police Delegates (ADPF) sent a formal letter to President Lula expressing 'extreme frustration' over the failure to fulfill former Justice Minister Ricardo Lewandowski's commitment to propose the creation of a National Fund to Combat Criminal Organizations. The union views the unfulfilled promise as a breach of agreements made at the end of last year.

item.title: Eleitor em Dia: saiba como verificar se seu título está regular
item.description: The deadline to regularize electoral status is May 6, when the voter registration closes. Voters can freely check their title status online via the Electoral Self-Service or the TSE Portal by providing title number, CPF, name, and birth date. The service allows users to identify pendencies, issue certificates, update data, and receive guidance for regularization.

item.title: Não é (só) a economia
item.description: Although only 9% cite the economy as the country's main problem, President Lula's approval is declining among economically active voters, particularly young and middle-aged adults. Trends show falling support for Lula and rising support for Flávio Bolsonaro, but the author cautions that, with six months until the election, the landscape remains highly volatile and subject to change through campaign messaging.

item.title: Tornozeleira neles
item.description: The Lula government has sanctioned two laws to combat femicide: one includes vicarious violence in the Maria da Penha Law with penalties of up to 40 years, and another regulates the use of electronic ankle monitors for aggressors, allowing delegates to impose them without judicial approval. Minister Márcia Lopes states that a national diagnosis was conducted to identify protection system flaws and that a bidding process is underway to equip police stations, especially in small cities. The National Pact Against Femicide was launched, involving the Executive, Legislative, and Judiciary branches, with an interinstitutional committee coordinated by the Secretariat of Institutional Relations.

item.title: Na mão grande
item.description: Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14.399 on March 31, 2026, establishing a national citizenship verification database for federal elections, aiming to centralize voter eligibility control in Washington. The measure, framed as preventing non-citizen voting, relies on error-prone and outdated federal databases to generate lists that may wrongfully exclude naturalized citizens, particularly Latinos and Brazilian permanent residents. Civil rights experts warn the system lacks transparency and could silently disenfranchise thousands of voters, echoing a prior attempt blocked by a federal judge for overstepping presidential authority and infringing on state and congressional powers over election rules.

item.title: Governo de São Paulo anuncia 1ª mulher no comando-geral da PM
item.description: São Paulo’s government appointed Colonel Glauce Anselmo Cavalli as the first woman to serve as commander-general of the state’s Military Police, the highest rank in the force. The appointment, published in the State Official Gazette on April 16, 2026, was praised by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas as a historic milestone and a step forward for women’s representation in state leadership. Cavalli succeeds Colonel José Augusto Coutinho, with Colonel Mário Kitsuwa named as her deputy commander.

item.title: Escala 6x1: equipe econômica descarta discutir contrapartidas às empresas; Motta e ministro da articulação política marcam reunião
item.description: The Lula government sent a bill to Congress to end the 6x1 work scale, but the economic team opposes financial compensation for companies, despite openness to transition rules. Rapporteur Paulo Azi suggested fiscal compensations to mitigate impacts, while opposition requested additional time for analysis. Chamber President Hugo Motta met with Minister José Guimarães to discuss the agenda.

item.title: Gestão Nunes acusa governo Lula de travar Faixa Azul para motos
item.description: The São Paulo City Hall accused the federal government of blocking the expansion of the Blue Lane, stating that the lack of approval prevents the delivery of 80 km of new exclusive motorcycle corridors. The Ricardo Nunes administration claims the obstacle is bureaucratic and harms urban mobility. The conflict arises amid tensions between the municipal and federal governments over transportation policies.

item.title: Planalto escala ministro para exaltar operação sobre o Master, mas enfrenta dilema sobre como abordar investigações
item.description: The Lula government deployed Justice Minister Wellington César Lima e Silva to comment on a Federal Police operation that arrested the former BRB president, Paulo Henrique, linked to the Banco Master scandal, as part of a Secom strategy to politically capitalize on the investigations and reinforce Lula’s narrative of fighting organized crime 'from the top'. However, government allies face a dilemma: while some advocate greater publicity to strengthen Lula’s anti-corruption image, others fear the case — particularly due to suspicions of STF ministers’ links to Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro — could further damage the president’s popularity, already weakened by rising anti-system sentiment.

item.title: Brasil responde a questões da gestão Trump sobre PIX, etanol e meio ambiente; negociações seguem
item.description: Brazil responded to all U.S. inquiries regarding PIX, ethanol, intellectual property, and environmental policies during meetings in Washington. The responses were technical and legal, with negotiations ongoing pending any further U.S. requests. The Brazilian government reiterated it will not alter the PIX system, as stated by President Lula.

item.title: Sóstenes quer usar documentário sobre Bolsonaro para fazer campanha para Flávio
item.description: Deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL-RJ), leader of the PL in the Chamber, stated at the premiere of the documentary "A Colisão dos Destinos" in Brasília that he intends to use the film about Jair Bolsonaro's political trajectory to boost the campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro, pre-candidate for President in 2026.

item.title: ‘Novo’ STF, privatização de tudo e flexibilização da CLT: o plano de governo de Romeu Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for presidency from the Novo party, unveiled a radical government plan proposing the reform of the Supreme Federal Court with ministerial terms, higher minimum age, and restrictions on relatives working in law firms, along with ending monocratic decisions. The plan also advocates for the privatization of all state-owned enterprises, fiscal austerity, tax cuts, and deepening labor flexibilization of the CLT, aligned with a Javier Milei-inspired minimal state agenda. The rhetoric emphasizes direct confrontation with institutions deemed 'untouchable' and promises a 'Brazil without untouchables'.

item.title: Lei institui Dia Nacional em Memória das Vítimas de Trânsito
item.description: Law 15.389 establishes the National Day in Memory of Traffic Victims, to be observed on May 7, aiming to honor victims and raise awareness about road safety. Signed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, the law originated from Bill 5.189/2019 by Senator Fabiano Contarato (PT-ES), approved by the Senate in 2022 and the Chamber of Deputies in March 2026. Contarato noted the date references a drunk-driving accident case in Curitiba, inspired by his 14 years as a traffic delegate witnessing families' grief.

item.title: Pré-estreia de filme sobre Bolsonaro em Brasília tem confusão, oração e ‘abraço de Ramagem’
item.description: The premiere of a documentary about Jair Bolsonaro in Brasília was marked by clashes with critics, a prayer in his favor, and a symbolic 'hug' from former deputy Alexandre Ramagem, recently released from U.S. detention. The event, hosted by the PL party leadership in Congress, included lawmakers and supporters, though none of Bolsonaro's children attended. Bolsonaro is serving a sentence under house arrest for attempted coup and related crimes.

item.title: Documentário sobre Bolsonaro será usado em campanha de Flávio, diz líder do PL
item.description: Deputy Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL-RJ) announced plans to use the documentary 'A Colisão dos Destinos', about Jair Bolsonaro, to boost Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential pre-candidacy through public screenings in squares and with sound trucks. The initiative raises concerns about potential early electioneering, though Cavalcante denies illegality, citing the film's pre-ineligibility production date. Experts warn the effort may blur the line between free expression and illicit electoral propaganda.

item.title: Galípolo apanha do lulismo
item.description: Allies of the Lula government criticize Central Bank president Gabriel Galípolo for maintaining high interest rates and for alleged closeness to financial markets, at the expense of coordination with the economic team. Dissatisfaction within the lulismo is growing, with figures like José Guimarães and Pedro Uczai pointing to a missed opportunity to cut the Selic rate and even expressing regret over Galípolo’s appointment. Criticisms also include alleged omissions in the Master case and unfavorable comparisons with former BC president Roberto Campos Neto.

item.title: Taxa das blusinhas: governo Lula avalia reduzir ou zerar alíquota para compras de até US$ 50
item.description: The Lula government is considering reducing or eliminating the 20% tax on international purchases under US$50, known as the 'blusinhas tax,' to boost the president's popularity amid rising competition from Flávio Bolsonaro. While the political wing pushes for full repeal to aid low-income consumers, the economic team and national retailers resist due to concerns over domestic industry impact. Lula confirmed changes will be announced in the coming weeks, with implementation after 40 days, though no specifics were disclosed.

item.title: Crusoé: Torres pede autorização para receber visita de Flávio na Papudinha
item.description: Former Justice Minister Anderson Torres requested authorization from Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes to receive a visit from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro at the Papudinha prison unit on April 29, from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Torres has been imprisoned since January 2023 for his role in the January 8 anti-democratic acts. The request pertains to a personal meeting between allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Ala do Novo quer aproximação entre Zema e Flávio e defende vice em chapa presidencial
item.description: A faction of the New Party is advocating for closer ties between former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), aiming for a potential presidential ticket with Zema as vice. Although Zema publicly denies abandoning his own candidacy, insiders say behind-the-scenes talks are ongoing to strengthen the party against the electoral threshold, particularly due to Zema’s vote potential in Minas Gerais.

item.title: Alcolumbre coloca advocacia do Senado ‘à disposição’ de parlamentares de CPI após embate com STF
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre offered institutional support from the Senate's Legal Advisory Office to senators involved in the Organized Crime Parliamentary Inquiry (CPI), following a confrontation with Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, who requested an investigation into Senator Alessandro Vieira for alleged abuse of authority. Vieira, the CPI rapporteur, had his report rejected after proposing the impeachment of STF ministers and the Prosecutor General, and warned of open threats from the Court against parliamentary functions. Alcolumbre stressed the defense of popular vote legitimacy and senators' prerogatives.

item.title: Cantor gospel que teve perfil suspenso por Moraes é pré-candidato a deputado federal
item.description: Gospel singer Davi Sacer announced his pre-candidacy for federal deputy in 2026 under the Progressistas (PP) party in São Paulo. His X (formerly Twitter) account was suspended in 2022 by order of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes after he posted the hotel address where Moraes and other justices were staying in New York, accompanied by a call for Brazilians to confront them. Sacer stated the suspension prompted deep reflection on freedom of expression and said his campaign is supported by family, pastors, and faith.

item.title: Ajuda de custo a paciente que se trata no SUS em outro município agora é lei
item.description: Law 15.390/2025 establishes the right to a cost allowance for SUS patients requiring out-of-municipality medical treatment (TFD), covering transportation, food, and lodging for the patient and a companion if needed. The benefit is discretionary, subject to budget availability, medical prescription, and authorization by municipal or state health managers, and does not apply to trips under 50 km or within the same metropolitan area. President Lula partially vetoed the bill, removing the provision for reimbursement of expenses if the allowance is not paid in a timely manner, citing legal uncertainty and potential increase in health-related litigation.

item.title: Alta nos preços dos combustíveis e endividamento viram munição usada pela oposição contra o governo nas redes sociais
item.description: The opposition, particularly the right, has been using rising fuel prices and growing Brazilian indebtedness as ammunition against the Lula government on social media, according to a study by Instituto Democracia em Xeque. The right accounted for 53% of tracked posts on the topic last week, compared to 29% for the left and 18% for the press. The discourse has expanded to include the impact on living costs, especially food prices, with figures like Flávio Bolsonaro and Thomas Abduch accusing the government of betraying workers and failing to deliver on promises.

item.title: Crusoé: Zema promete um novo STF
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) promised to create a 'new Supreme Federal Court' if elected, stating its members should be accountable for their actions. He presented this proposal as the first act of his future government plan in an interview released on Thursday, the 16th.
